source.title: GAVEL: Towards rule-based safety through activation monitoring
source.authors: Shir Rozenfeld; Rahul Pankajakshan; Itay Zloczower; Eyal Lenga; Gilad Gressel; Yisroel Mirsky

record.file_problem: The full paper and appendices are present. A localized passage around the page 9 figures contains garbled characters; this does not prevent reading the study's main text or relevant appendix.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies activation-based detection and reports co-detection of cognitive elements, but does not test superposition, capacity pressure, neuron polysemanticity, SAE feature recovery or feature dimensionality.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that multiple cognitive-element (CE) detector outputs overlap, but this is not a measurement of feature directions, their geometry, or capacity competition. The detector is trained on deliberately elicited CEs, and its overlap results therefore do not establish naturally occurring superposition. The discussion of SAEs is background, not a test of SAE features as canonical units.
record.test_reason: GAVEL trains supervised multi-label classifiers on attention outputs to detect deliberately elicited 'cognitive elements' for safety monitoring. It reports detector TPR/FPR, not feature geometry, neuron polysemanticity, capacity allocation, SAE feature recovery or feature dimensionality. SAEs are mentioned only as related work and future work (Bricken et al., Cunningham et al.). No result bears on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that compositional rules over cognitive elements give precise, configurable, interpretable activation-based safety detection. They report it beats baselines (AUC ~0.99, near-zero FPR on Mistral-7B), is robust to text-level adversarial attacks, and transfers across models and languages.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes and evaluates an activation-based safety detector and rule framework, not the original toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that detector performance varies with activation source (attention outputs versus hidden states) and layer range; these ablations concern CE detection, not the claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: A multi-label CE detector trained only on isolated-CE excitation data flags multiple CEs on the same tokens. This occurs in 54% of evaluated dialogues.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Supervised probes trained on isolated concepts can co-detect several concepts on one token in LLM activations. This is detector-output co-occurrence, not evidence about the geometry of superposed features.

record.problems: The paper does not measure the geometrical properties, dimensionality or capacity allocation relevant to the claim. Its CE datasets and misuse conversations are deliberately elicited or generated, and the reported co-occurrence is based on detector outputs rather than direct feature-geometry measurements.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, no sparsity sweep, no feature geometry.
All: no neuron-level polysemanticity or capacity allocation analysis.
All: no analysis of the causes of polysemanticity.
All: no measurement of features spread across neurons; no SAE trained or evaluated.
All: concepts are detected with GRU classifiers over stacked layers; the dimensionality of features is not examined.

record.verdict_notes: The relation was changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only'. The paper only references SAEs and superposition-adjacent work in background and future work, and makes no specific argument about any version. The authors' wording that the classifier 'disentangles' overlapping concepts is informal and is not a superposition test.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, sparse feature counts relative to dimensions, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions and regular geometry.
Neuron polysemanticity, capacity competition, and the proposed allocation of dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure or whether polysemanticity evidences superposition.
Whether LLM features spread across neurons or whether SAEs recover sparse features.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical units of model representation.
Whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional.

rows.subject: evaluation-set conversations
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed dialogue and token-level simultaneous CE-detector activations.

conditions.value: evaluation set; dialogue categories and sample count for this analysis not stated
multi-label CE classifier; thresholds not stated

rows.measure: Share of dialogues containing tokens where multiple CEs exceeded their detection thresholds simultaneously
rows.locator: Appendix C, Analysis of CE Co-occurrence; also Section 3.0.2
rows.note: Aggregate result. This is co-detection by the trained CE classifier, not a measurement of feature-direction geometry or capacity pressure; it does not establish the superposition claim.
rows.check: The 54% figure counts dialogues with tokens where several trained CE detector outputs exceeded threshold at once. It is a co-detection rate from a supervised classifier, not a measure of superposed feature directions, interference geometry or capacity. Its baseline is unstated. Section 3.0.2 says the 54% is of 'detected malicious dialogues', while Appendix C says 'all conversations in our evaluation set'. The denominator is therefore inconsistent.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
